:::{#thm-symmetric-bilinear-form-swap}
#### A symmetric bilinear form does not depend on the order of its vectors

If $\matr{A}$ is a $p \times p$ [symmetric matrix](#def-symmetric-matrix),
then its [bilinear form](#def-bilinear-form) is the same with its vectors swapped,
[for all](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/proof-writing.html#def-universal-quantifier) $\vx, \vy \in \reals^p$:

$$
\bform{\matr{A}}{\vy}{\vx} = \bform{\matr{A}}{\vx}{\vy}.
$$

:::

::: proof

The second step uses the fact that
[a $1 \times 1$ product equals its own transpose](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#thm-scalar-transpose):

$$
\ba
\bform{\matr{A}}{\vy}{\vx}
&= \tp{\vy}\, \matr{A}\, \vx
&& \text{(@def-bilinear-form)}
\\
&= \tp{\vx}\, \tp{\matr{A}}\, \vy
&& \text{(a } 1 \times 1 \text{ product equals its own transpose)}
\\
&= \tp{\vx}\, \matr{A}\, \vy
&& \text{(@def-symmetric-matrix)}
\\
&= \bform{\matr{A}}{\vx}{\vy}.
&& \text{(@def-bilinear-form)}
\ea
$$

:::
